text:
sam: Heads-up — merged PR #4823 changed the attention kernel selector. Canary is showing a decode p95 spike for short-seq traffic (~1.8x). Anyone else seeing this?
anya: Yup, repro on our perf canary. Shortseq p95 jumped from ~38ms -> ~70ms. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/canary/shortseq (internal)
noah: I profiled the canary run. Flamegraph points to an extra memcpy in the KV path right after kernel switch, and the fused-attn path seems to be getting a fallback path that does an extra copy.
luis: FWIW, the selector change prefers the fused-matmul kernel for most shapes now. Looks like when KV cache is present we sometimes end up with a shape-mismatch path that forces a copy+fallback.
sam: So this is selector-induced, not purely batching? Could be an interaction with microbatching thresholds.
anya: CI also flagged it — job 870 had decode_tail_p95 up 61%, tolerance exceeded.
ci-bot: CI PERF REGRESSION: job 870 - decode_tail_p95 increased 61% (baseline=42ms -> 68ms). See: https://ci.redwood/job/870
noah: Quick bisect idea: revert the kernel-selector change (commit 7f3d2aa) or apply a short-seq heuristic to prefer the legacy kernel for seq_len < 32. That should tell us whether selector is root cause.
emma: I captured a trace from the canary instance; snippet below:
```
[2026-03-20T03:12:01Z] request id=abc123 seq_len=18 kv_present=true
kernel_select: prefused_matmul -> compile_path
kv_sync: memcpy 1.2ms
fused_attn_wrapper: fallback_to_generic +2.1ms (memcopy)
decode_tail: p95 add 28ms
```
luis: Looks like microbatch jitter is delaying flushes so more requests hit the cached-KV path unexpectedly, exacerbating the fallback. Batcher threshold tweak in PR #4801 changed the flush boundary too. Two changes combined may be the ripple.
anya: Repro steps I used: `make perf-harness && ./harness --scenario=shortseq_kv --iters=200 --batch=adaptive`
sam: Can someone run a quick revert on staging? If reverting the selector eliminates the spike we should hot-revert and then fix properly.
luis: I can run the revert canary in ~30m. Quick local patch I tested: in kernel_selector.cpp add early-return for short sequences when kv_cache_active:
```c++
if (kv_cache_active && seq_len < 32) return legacy_attn_kernel;
```
This dropped p95 back to ~40ms locally.
emma: If we revert, we need to pin the rollout and stop auto-promote for the current release candidate. deploy-bot, can you schedule a controlled canary?
deploy-bot: Scheduled rolling canary deploy (hot-revert candidate) to 3 canary hosts at 03:30 UTC. Approval needed from @sam and @anya.
sam: Approved. :thumbsup: Hold the full rollout until canary metrics look stable for 1 hour. @luis please run the perf harness against canary and paste numbers.
luis: Running now. Command I used: `cargo run --bin perf-harness -- --scenario shortseq_kv --iters 1000`. Will post results in 10m.
luis: Canary results after revert candidate: decode_tail_p95 = 40ms (was 68ms on problematic canary). Throughput similar. Looks good.
sam: Please open the revert PR and tag it `rollback=true` so release sees it. We'll revert first, then follow up with a proper fix.
noah: Follow-up I’ll own: dig into why the fused path falls back and why an extra memcpy is introduced. My hypothesis: prefetch/memcpy ordering assumes a fused kernel path that we now occasionally skip, leaving a stray memmove.
emma: Also adding a perf CI gate for shortseq_kv decode_tail_p95 so future selector changes can't land blind.
sam: Thanks team. Moving to revert PR: 5301234578. After revert merges, we'll add unit tests for kernel selection + kv cache combos and a perf test. Closing triage until revert completes. :white_check_mark:
